mainTopic: How the קרבנות of מוסף and שבועות hold each other back, and how the hard פסוקים of יחזקאל fit the תורה
overview: The amud begins by asking which rams the משנה means when it says the bulls, rams and sheep do not hold each other back. The גמרא answers that the rams of ויקרא and the ram of במדבר do not hold each other back, and that the תנא gives each animal its own rule. A ברייתא then explains why יחזקאל lists fewer animals for ראש חודש than the תורה does. When the full number cannot be found, you bring what you can, even one lamb, but you still try for as many as possible. The word 'יהיו' teaches when offerings do hold each other back. The גמרא then works through several hard פסוקים in יחזקאל that seem to clash with the תורה: a bull called a חטאת, נבלה forbidden only to כהנים, and offerings on 'the seventh of the month.' Each one gets an explanation that fits the תורה. רב praises חנינא בן חזקיה, who explained these פסוקים and so kept ספר יחזקאל from being hidden away. Finally, the גמרא returns to רבי שמעון in the משנה. His source teaches that it is better to bring one bull with its נסכים than many bulls without them, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Which rams does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which אילים the משנה has in mind, since neither option seems to fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rams from which place? If it means those of the מוספין, there is only one ram there. If it means the rams of עצרת in תורת כהנים, the Torah writes a word of 'being' (יהיו) about them, so they must be brought exactly as written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's word 'rams' (plural). It cannot find a group of rams that fits the rule 'they do not hold each other back.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מוספין of ראש חודש and עצרת in חומש הפקודים have only one איל, so there are no 'rams' there to hold each other back. The two rams that come with the שתי הלחם in תורת כהנים are described with 'יהיו', and a word of הויה means the details are required (מעכב). So no group of rams can fit the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rams (plural)
שבועות, the festival of the 'gathering'
The book of ויקרא
A word of 'being' such as 'יהיו'. It shows the detail is required.

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different sets of קרבנות on שבועות. The מוסף of the day is in במדבר and has one ram. The קרבנות that come with the שתי הלחם are in ויקרא and have two rams. Keep them apart.

phrases.english: Rams of where?
If those [of the additional offerings], it is a single ram,
if those of Shavuot in Leviticus –
a term of 'being' is written about them.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the משנה's mention of rams.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the אילים do not hold each other back.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither possible set of rams fits. The מוספין have only one ram. The rams of תורת כהנים are required because of the word הויה.

steps.title: The rams of Leviticus and the ram of Numbers do not hold each other back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה means the rams of תורת כהנים. Its rule is about the two sets of rams in relation to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it means the rams of עצרת in תורת כהנים, and this is what the משנה is saying: the rams of תורת כהנים do not hold back the ram of חומש הפקודים, and the ram of חומש הפקודים does not hold back the rams of תורת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה does mean the rams of תורת כהנים. 'Not holding back' is about the two separate sets, not about the rams inside one set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הויה only makes the two rams of ויקרא required for each other. It says nothing about how they relate to the מוסף ram in במדבר. So the משנה's rule is true between the sets: missing one set does not stop you from bringing the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (keeping the original option)
They hold back (one cannot be brought without the other)
The book of במדבר

phrases.english: Actually, it means those of Shavuot in Leviticus,
and this is what it is saying:
neither do the rams of Leviticus
prevent the ram of the book of Numbers,
nor does the ram of the book of Numbers
prevent the rams of Leviticus.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דַּעֲצֶרֶת דְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the scope of the משנה's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה meant that the rams inside one set do not hold each other back.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means that the rams of ויקרא and the ram of במדבר, as two sets, do not hold each other back.

steps.title: The משנה's list becomes uneven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this answer gives the bulls and the rams in the same list two different kinds of rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then: the bulls do not hold back even each other, while the rams only fail to hold back the rams of here and there, but they themselves (inside their own set) do hold each other back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 2. It now gives the items listed together in the משנה very different meanings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the bulls, 'not holding back' means even the bulls in one set are not needed for each other. For the rams, the answer from step 2 means only the two sets are separate, while the two rams of ויקרא do hold each other back. It seems odd for one list in the משנה to mean two different things.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulls
Each other
Here and there (the two books)

phrases.english: But then, bulls –
that do not prevent even each other,
and rams –
it is those of here and there that do not prevent,
but they themselves do prevent?
phrases.notes: The two rams of ויקרא still hold each other back, because of the word הויה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One list in the משנה would carry two different meanings of 'not holding back.'

steps.title: Each item has its own rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תנא teaches each item in the list with its own separate rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא teaches item by item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the list is uneven. It explains that the משנה teaches each animal's law on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being listed together in one line does not mean the items share one rule. The bulls follow their rule and the rams follow theirs, so the answer from step 2 stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה
He teaches separate matters, each one on its own

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה means the rams of ויקרא and the ram of במדבר do not hold each other back. Inside the ויקרא set, the two rams do hold each other back because of הויה. Each item in the משנה's list has its own rule.

phrases.english: The tanna teaches matter by matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the uneven reading by explaining how the משנה is written
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Items listed together in the משנה must share one meaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא teaches each item on its own, so the bulls and the rams can have different rules.

steps.title: Why does יחזקאל say only one bull?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes יחזקאל's ראש חודש offering and asks why it says 'a bull' in the singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And on the day of the New Moon, a young bull without blemish, and six lambs and a ram, they shall be without blemish.' Why does it say 'a bull'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that quotes a פסוק in יחזקאל about the ראש חודש offerings. It asks why that פסוק mentions only one bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the תורה, the ראש חודש offering has two bulls. יחזקאל mentions just one, so the two lists look like they disagree. The ברייתא is setting up an answer that will explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Moon, the start of a Jewish month, which has its own special offerings
A young bull
Lambs
Why does the פסוק say this? What is it coming to teach?

steps.confusionAlert: This פסוק is from יחזקאל, not from the חומש. The question exists only because the תורה gives a different number.

phrases.english: "And on the day of the New Moon (you shall take)
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 46:6. The word in round brackets is in some versions, but it isn't in the פסוק itself.

phrases.english: a young bull without blemish
and six lambs and a ram
they shall be without blemish."
"A bull": why does the verse say this?
phrases.notes: The question is about the singular. The תורה (במדבר 28:11) says two bulls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא opens a new discussion about יחזקאל's ראש חודש offering.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is יחזקאל teaching by mentioning one bull, when the תורה requires two?

steps.title: If two bulls cannot be found, bring one
steps.stepSummary: The single bull teaches that if two bulls are not available, one bull is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the תורה says 'bulls,' how do we know that if he could not find two, he brings one? The פסוק says 'a bull.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: יחזקאל says 'a bull' to teach that one bull may be brought when two cannot be found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading only the תורה, we might think that without two bulls the offering cannot be brought at all. יחזקאל's singular 'bull' teaches a fallback: bring the one you have. So the two פסוקים do not disagree. The תורה gives the full requirement, and יחזקאל gives what to do when the full number isn't available.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulls (plural), the תורה's wording
And from where do we know?
He did not find, meaning the animals were not available

phrases.english: Since it is said in the Torah "bulls,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:11

phrases.english: from where do we know that if he did not find two
he brings one?
The verse says "a bull."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יחזקאל's 'a bull' teaches that if two bulls cannot be found, one is brought.

steps.title: Why does יחזקאל say only six lambs?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא moves to the next part of the פסוק and asks why it mentions six lambs.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Six lambs': why does the פסוק say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks the same kind of question about the lambs: why does יחזקאל say six?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires seven lambs on ראש חודש, but יחזקאל says six. This is the same pattern as the bull question, so we can expect the same kind of answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Six
Seven, the number of lambs the תורה requires

phrases.english: "Six lambs": why does the verse say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question as step 5, now on the lambs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is יחזקאל teaching by mentioning six lambs, when the תורה requires seven?

steps.title: If seven lambs cannot be found, bring six
steps.stepSummary: Six lambs teaches that when seven are not available, six are brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the תורה says 'seven,' how do we know that if he could not find seven, he brings six? The פסוק says 'six.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the lamb question the same way it answered the bull question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's 'seven' could make us think that six lambs are worthless. יחזקאל's 'six' teaches that if seven aren't available, six should still be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written in the תורה
He should bring

phrases.english: Since it is written in the Torah "seven,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:11

phrases.english: from where do we know that if he did not find seven
he should bring six?
The verse says "six."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יחזקאל's 'six lambs' teaches that if seven cannot be found, six are brought.

steps.title: Bring as many lambs as you can, even one
steps.stepSummary: A later פסוק teaches that you can go all the way down, even to one lamb, according to what is available.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that if he could not find six, he brings five; if not five, four; if not four, three; if not three, two; and even one? The פסוק says: 'And for the lambs, as his means suffice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes one step further. It asks how we know that we can go below six, all the way to one lamb, and answers from the next פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Six' alone only teaches that six is acceptable instead of seven. To allow any smaller number, the ברייתא uses the phrase 'as his means suffice,' which means bringing whatever he is able to get. This finishes the ברייתא's rule: the תורה's numbers are the ideal, but when they can't be met, you bring as many as you can.

keyTerms.meaning: As his means suffice: whatever he is able to get
And even one
And for the lambs

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה gives the full numbers for the ראש חודש offering: two bulls and seven lambs. יחזקאל's smaller numbers teach that when the full count isn't available, you bring what you can, even a single lamb.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם לֹא מָצָא שִׁשָּׁה, יָבִיא חֲמִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: And from where do we know that if he did not find six, he should bring five;
if not five, he should bring four;
phrases.notes: Each time, 'if he did not find' is understood: no five, so bring four, and so on.

phrases.english: if not four, he should bring three;
if not three, he should bring two;
and even one?
The verse says: "And for the lambs as his means suffice."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 46:7

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם לֹא מָצָא שִׁשָּׁה, יָבִיא חֲמִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule of step 8 further, allowing any smaller number down to one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'As his means suffice' teaches that whatever number of lambs is available, even one, is brought.

steps.title: Why say 'six lambs' if even one is enough?
steps.stepSummary: Step 9 taught that even one lamb is enough. So why does the פסוק need to mention six lambs at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the later פסוק already teaches that you bring whatever you can, even one lamb, why do I need the words 'six lambs'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the 'six lambs' teaching from step 8. If the later פסוק already lets you go down to one lamb, the 'six' detail seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 learned from 'six lambs' that you bring six if you don't have seven. Step 9 learned that you can go all the way down to one. If one is fine, then six adds nothing new, so the גמרא asks what 'six' is there for.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is already written this way
Why do I need it? (asking what a word or detail adds)
Lambs

phrases.english: But since it is written this way,
phrases.notes: He means the later פסוק from step 9, which lets you bring as many lambs as you can, even one.

phrases.english: why do I need "six lambs"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר דִּכְתִיב הָכִי, ״שִׁשָּׁה כְּבָשִׂים״ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the need for step 8's teaching in light of step 9's teaching.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even one lamb is enough (step 9), the 'six lambs' rule seems to add nothing.

steps.title: We still try to bring as many as possible
steps.stepSummary: 'Six lambs' teaches that even though one is enough, we should try to bring as many as we can.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that as much as it is possible to try for more, we try.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: 'six lambs' teaches that we should make an effort to get as many lambs as possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One lamb is the bare minimum that still counts. But the 'six' detail teaches that we should not settle for less when more is available. So the two teachings do different jobs: one sets the minimum, the other sets the goal.

keyTerms.meaning: To seek out, to make an effort to get
We seek out, we go out of our way (related to the word הידור)
That it is possible

steps.whatToRemember: One lamb is enough to count, but we try to bring as many of the seven as we can get.

phrases.english: That as much as it is possible to seek out more,
we seek them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra detail a separate purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since one lamb is enough, 'six lambs' seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Six lambs' teaches we should try for as many as possible, even though one counts.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the animals hold each other back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the required animals hold each other back, meaning all must be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know (about the rams in תורת כהנים) that they hold each other back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and is setting up the next step: what is the source that these offerings hold each other back?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was showing how you can bring fewer animals. Now it asks about a case where the offerings do hold each other back, so missing one stops the מצוה from being done properly. It wants a פסוק for that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
They hold each other back (each one is needed, so missing one stops the others from counting)
The book of ויקרא (literally 'the teaching of the כהנים')
Rams

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the steps before. There, fewer animals were allowed. Here the question is about offerings where every animal is required.

phrases.english: And from where do we know
(regarding the rams in תורת כהנים)
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in round brackets and some leave them out.

phrases.english: that they hold each other back?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן (לְאֵילִים שֶׁבְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים) שֶׁמְּעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from offerings that may be reduced to offerings that hold each other back.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that these offerings hold each other back.

steps.title: The word 'יהיו' teaches they must all be brought
steps.stepSummary: The word 'יהיו' ('they shall be') shows the offerings must be brought exactly as written.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'they shall be.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source: the פסוק says 'יהיו', meaning the animals must be brought exactly as commanded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יהיו' is read as 'they must be this way.' That wording makes the full list required, so if one animal is missing, the rest do not count properly.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches by saying...
'They shall be': read as 'it must be exactly this way'

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'יהיו' is a signal that something is required, so the offerings hold each other back.

phrases.english: The verse says "they shall be."
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:31

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'יהיו' teaches that the offerings hold each other back.

steps.title: יחזקאל calls the ראש חודש bull a חטאת, but it is an עולה
steps.stepSummary: יחזקאל's ראש חודש ניסן bull is described with the word for חטאת, but the Torah's ראש חודש bulls are עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'So says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first of the month, you shall take a young bull without blemish, and you shall purify the Sanctuary.' 'A חטאת'? It is an עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a hard פסוק in יחזקאל and points out that it seems to contradict the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וחטאת' ('and you shall purify') comes from the word חטאת, so it sounds like the bull is a חטאת. But the Torah says the bulls of ראש חודש are brought as an עולה. So the פסוק seems to clash with the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall purify (same root as חטאת)
Sin offering
Burnt offering
A young bull

phrases.english: "So says the Lord God:
In the first month, on the first of the month,
you shall take a young bull without blemish,
and you shall purify the Sanctuary."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 45:18

phrases.english: "A sin offering"? It is a burnt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: another difficult פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק implies a חטאת, but the Torah's ראש חודש bulls are an עולה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: אליהו will explain it in the future
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן admits the passage is hard and says אליהו הנביא will explain it in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This passage, אליהו will explain it in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן responds to the question. He does not solve it; he says the answer will come when אליהו explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an honest admission that רבי יוחנן has no clear answer to the problem. He leaves the explanation for the future, and step 16 brings רב אשי's actual answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A passage or section of a פסוק
אליהו will explain it in the future

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real solution. רבי יוחנן is saying the question is too hard to answer now.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
This passage, Elijah will explain it in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 14 by leaving the difficulty for the future.
steps.terutzResolutionType: No answer for now; the explanation is left to אליהו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק contradicts the Torah's ראש חודש offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוחנן, the difficulty waits for אליהו to explain it. Step 16 gives רב אשי's answer.

steps.title: רב אשי: it is about the מילואים of עזרא's time
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the פסוק is not about the regular ראש חודש offering but about special inauguration offerings in the days of עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: They brought inauguration offerings in the days of עזרא, just as they brought them in the days of משה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a real answer: the bull in the פסוק was part of special inauguration offerings, not the regular ראש חודש offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the inauguration of the משכן in the days of משה, a חטאת bull was brought. רב אשי says that in the days of עזרא they did the same kind of inauguration, so the bull in יחזקאל really is a חטאת. Since it is not the ראש חודש עולה, there is no contradiction with the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The inauguration offerings, brought when the service in the משכן or מקדש first began
They offered, they brought as a קרבן
In the same way as

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי solves the contradiction: the bull in יחזקאל was a חטאת of the מילואים in עזרא's time, not the ראש חודש עולה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common way to answer a contradiction: show that the פסוק is talking about a different event, so it does not clash with the Torah's rule.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
They brought inauguration offerings in the days of Ezra,
just as they brought them in the days of Moses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מִילּוּאִים הִקְרִיבוּ בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 14, instead of leaving it open like רבי יוחנן in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the פסוק in a different setting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bull is the regular ראש חודש offering, which is an עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bull is a חטאת of the מילואים in the days of עזרא, like the inauguration in the days of משה.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up both earlier answers about יחזקאל's bull
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the same two approaches. רבי יהודה says אליהו will explain the passage, and רבי יוסי says it describes the מלואים offerings of עזרא's time. רבי יהודה then accepts רבי יוסי's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, 'אליהו will explain this passage in the future.' רבי יוסי said to him, 'They brought inauguration offerings in the days of עזרא, just as they brought them in the days of משה.' רבי יהודה said to him, 'May your mind be at rest, because you have put my mind at rest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the answers of רבי יוחנן and רב אשי were already said by earlier sages. רבי יהודה says the same thing as רבי יוחנן, and רבי יוסי says the same thing as רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה at first gives up on explaining the passage. רבי יוסי says the bull in יחזקאל was a one-time חטאת brought when the second בית המקדש was inaugurated, just like the מלואים in משה's time. So it does not clash with the regular ראש חודש עולות. רבי יהודה's warm reply shows he fully accepts this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way: a ברייתא that supports what was just said
Inauguration offerings, brought when the משכן or בית המקדש was first started
In the days of עזרא, when the second בית המקדש was built
May your mind be at rest, a blessing of thanks for a good explanation

steps.whatToRemember: The bull in יחזקאל that is called a חטאת was a special, one-time inauguration offering in עזרא's time. It was not the regular ראש חודש offering, so there is no clash with the Torah.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא:
רבי יהודה says:
This passage, אליהו will explain in the future.
רבי יוסי said to him:
They brought inauguration offerings in the days of עזרא,
just as they brought them in the days of משה.
He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here רבי יהודה is answering רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: May your mind be at rest, because you have put my mind at rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports both רבי יוחנן's answer (step 15) and רב אשי's answer (step 16) with an earlier ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The two answers to the problem of יחזקאל's ראש חודש bull, especially רב אשי's answer that it was a special inauguration offering
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the exchange between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי

steps.title: Why does יחזקאל forbid נבלה and טרפה only to כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: יחזקאל says the כהנים may not eat נבלה or טרפה. That seems to imply ordinary Jews may eat them, but the Torah forbids them to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The כהנים shall not eat any נבלה or טרפה, whether bird or animal.' Is it only the כהנים who may not eat these, so ordinary Jews may eat them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new hard פסוק in יחזקאל and asks a question about it. Since the פסוק mentions only כהנים, it sounds as if everyone else is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids נבלה and טרפה to every Jew. So singling out כהנים seems either pointless or misleading. The challenge is: what does the word 'כהנים' add?

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
An animal with a fatal injury or defect, which is forbidden to eat
But this implies…, used to draw out what a statement suggests

phrases.english: 'And any נבלה or טרפה,'
whether bird or animal,
the כהנים shall not eat.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:31

phrases.english: Is it only כהנים who may not eat these,
but ordinary Jews may eat them?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים הוּא דְּלֹא יֹאכְלוּ, הָא יִשְׂרָאֵל אָכְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new hard פסוק in יחזקאל, in the same style as the earlier ראש חודש bull problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: יחזקאל 44:31, which forbids נבלה and טרפה specifically to כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming only כהנים suggests that ordinary Jews are allowed, which goes against the Torah's ban on everyone.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: אליהו will explain this passage
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן admits this פסוק is hard and leaves its explanation for אליהו in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: אליהו will explain this passage in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the same kind of answer he gave for the ראש חודש bull. He admits the problem and leaves it for אליהו to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a real solution. It admits that the פסוק is hard but does not doubt that it fits with the Torah. Just like before, a later אמורא will offer an actual explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A passage or section of פסוקים
אליהו הנביא, who will come before משיח and settle hard questions
Will explain it in the future

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
This passage, אליהו will explain in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge of step 18 by putting off the explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admits the difficulty and leaves it for אליהו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to permit נבלה and טרפה to ordinary Jews.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוחנן, the פסוק will be explained in the future. Step 20 gives רבינא's actual explanation.

steps.title: רבינא: the פסוק is needed because of מליקה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that כהנים needed their own warning. Since כהנים may eat a bird killed by מליקה, we might have thought נבלה and טרפה are also permitted to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The פסוק needed to mention כהנים. You might have thought that since מליקה is permitted to them, נבלה and טרפה are also permitted to them. So the פסוק teaches us that they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a real explanation. The פסוק is not saying ordinary Jews may eat נבלה. It is stopping a mistake that could have happened specifically about כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird חטאת is killed by מליקה, pinching the neck, not by שחיטה. Outside the מקדש, that would make the bird a נבלה. Yet כהנים eat it. So one could think כהנים are not bound by the נבלה rules at all, and יחזקאל's פסוק teaches that they are.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed, meaning the פסוק has a purpose
You might have thought: introduces a mistaken idea the פסוק comes to block
Killing a bird offering by having the כהן pinch its neck with his fingernail
It teaches us: the פסוק tells us otherwise

steps.whatToRemember: יחזקאל's ban is aimed at כהנים because מליקה could have made us think the נבלה rules don't apply to them. It does not mean ordinary Jews are allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: מליקה does not make the bird a נבלה. The Torah made it the proper way to kill a bird offering. That is exactly why someone could wrongly conclude that כהנים are free from the נבלה rules in general.

phrases.english: רבינא said:
It needed to mention כהנים,
because it could have entered your mind to say:
since מליקה is permitted for them,
phrases.notes: He means כהנים may eat a bird חטאת killed by pinching, even though it had no שחיטה.

phrases.english: נבלה and טרפה should also be permitted to them,
so it teaches us that they are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an actual explanation in place of רבי יוחנן's 'אליהו will explain,' just as רב אשי did in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the פסוק needs to mention כהנים (a צריכותא answer)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מליקה is permitted to כהנים, נבלה and טרפה would be permitted to them too.
steps.terutzMaskana: כהנים are also forbidden in נבלה and טרפה. The פסוק does not suggest that ordinary Jews are allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern: when a פסוק names one group, it may simply be blocking a mistake about that group, not giving permission to everyone else.

steps.title: What is 'the seventh of the month' in יחזקאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a third hard פסוק in יחזקאל, which talks about offerings on the seventh of the month, and asks what 'seventh' could mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And so shall you do on the seventh of the month for one who sins by mistake and for one who is simple, and you shall atone for the House.' Why 'seventh'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new difficulty, setting up the next discussion. It quotes the פסוק and asks what 'the seventh of the month' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah has no special offerings on the seventh day of any month. So a פסוק in יחזקאל that orders atonement offerings 'on the seventh' seems to have no source in the Torah. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh day of the month
One who sins by mistake
A simple, naive person
And you shall atone

phrases.english: 'And so shall you do on the seventh of the month
for one who sins by mistake and for one who is simple,
and you shall atone for the House.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 45:20

phrases.english: 'Seventh'? What does that mean?
phrases.notes: The puzzle is that no offerings are set for the seventh of any month in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a third hard פסוק in יחזקאל, after the נבלה and טרפה question is settled.
steps.kashyaTarget: יחזקאל 45:20, which speaks of atonement offerings on the seventh of the month
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah sets no offerings for the seventh of any month, so the פסוק seems to have no basis in the Torah.

steps.title: Seven means seven tribes who sinned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that 'seventh' in the פסוק refers to seven tribes who sinned by following a mistaken court ruling. That counts as a communal sin even if they are not most of the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: these are seven tribes who sinned, even though they are not the majority of the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 21 about what 'seventh' means. רבי יוחנן says it means seven tribes who sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as being about the bull brought when the community sins by following a mistaken court ruling. The 'seven' is seven tribes, which is most of the tribes. Then it counts as a sin of the whole community, even if the number of people who sinned is not most of the nation.

keyTerms.meaning: Seven tribes, which is a majority of the twelve tribes
The majority of the congregation, meaning most of the people
Who sinned

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'seventh' here as a date. רבי יוחנן turns the number into a count of tribes, not a day of the month.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
These are seven tribes who sinned,
phrases.notes: He is explaining the word 'seventh' from the פסוק in Step 21 (יחזקאל 45:20).

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רוּבָּהּ שֶׁל קָהָל.
phrases.english: even though they are not the majority of the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵלּוּ שִׁבְעָה שְׁבָטִים שֶׁחָטְאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21 about the meaning of 'seventh'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק a new way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Seventh of the month' seems to be a date for extra offerings that the Torah never mentions.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Seven' means seven tribes who sinned, so the פסוק is about the bull brought for a communal sin.

steps.title: Month means a new ruling, and errs means a mistake together with an action
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's reading continues. 'Month' (חודש) hints that the court made up something new (חידשו), like permitting forbidden fat. 'One that errs' teaches that the bull is brought only when the court's mistake leads the people to act by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Month': if they made up something new and said forbidden fat is permitted. 'For every one that errs and for him that is simple': this teaches that they are only liable for a matter hidden from the court, together with an action done by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the rest of the פסוק along the lines of רבי יוחנן's explanation. Each word now points to a rule about the bull brought for a communal mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חודש is read like חידשו, 'they made up something new', meaning the court ruled against the Torah, for example that חלב is permitted. The words 'one that errs' teach a condition: the court must have made a mistake (העלם דבר), and the people must also have acted on it by mistake (שגגת מעשה). With this, the whole פסוק fits the Torah's law and no longer clashes with it.

keyTerms.meaning: They made up something new, here a new ruling that goes against the Torah
Forbidden animal fat
A matter hidden from the court, meaning the court made a mistaken ruling
An action done by mistake, when the people act on the wrong ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that the communal bull needs both parts: a mistaken ruling by the court and a mistaken action by the people.

phrases.english: "Month":
phrases.notes: The word חודש sounds like חידשו, 'they made up something new'. That is the play on words here.

phrases.english: if they made up something new and said
that forbidden fat is permitted,
"For every one that errs and for him that is simple":
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 45:20

phrases.english: this teaches that they are not liable
except for a matter hidden from the court
together with an action done by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's reading from Step 22 through the rest of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading each word of the פסוק as a hint to a known law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Month' seems to be a date and 'one that errs' seems to describe an atonement offering that the Torah does not have for that day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words describe the rules of the communal bull: a new mistaken ruling, followed by the people's mistaken action.

steps.title: Praise for חנינא בן חזקיה, who saved ספר יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רב praises חנינא בן חזקיה. Without him, ספר יחזקאל would have been hidden away because it seemed to contradict the Torah. He took 300 jugs of oil up to his upper room and worked out the meaning of all the hard verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says in the name of רב: That man is remembered for good, and חנינא בן חזקיה is his name. Were it not for him, ספר יחזקאל would have been hidden away, because its words contradicted the words of the Torah. What did he do? He brought up three hundred jugs of oil, sat in the upper room, and interpreted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its discussion of the hard verses in יחזקאל with a general statement. It praises the man who showed that the book does not really contradict the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last few steps showed verses in יחזקאל that seemed to clash with the Torah. רב says the danger was real: the book could have been hidden away (נגנז). חנינא בן חזקיה worked so hard, using enough oil to learn day and night, that he found explanations for all of them, so the book was kept.

keyTerms.meaning: Remembered for good, a phrase of praise
Hidden away, meaning not kept as part of the holy books
Contradicting
Jugs of oil, used for light
An upper room

steps.whatToRemember: The hard verses in יחזקאל are not real contradictions. They can be explained to fit the Torah, as חנינא בן חזקיה showed, and the explanations we just learned are examples of this.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
That man is remembered for good,
and Chanina ben Chizkiya is his name,
for were it not for him,
the book of Yechezkel would have been hidden away,
because its words contradicted the words of the Torah.
What did he do?
He brought up three hundred jugs of oil,
and sat in the upper room and interpreted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זָכוּר אוֹתוֹ הָאִישׁ לַטּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole discussion of hard verses in יחזקאל with a general statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ספר יחזקאל was kept because חנינא בן חזקיה explained how its hard verses fit the Torah.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי שמעון on having many bulls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the opening of רבי שמעון's statement: if they had many bulls. It is setting up a discussion of his opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: If they had many bulls, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of יחזקאל and goes back to the משנה. It quotes the opening words of רבי שמעון to set up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic. In the משנה, רבי שמעון talks about a case where they had many bulls for the day's offerings. The 'etc.' means the rest of his words in the משנה is assumed, and the discussion of it comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Many bulls
Etc., meaning the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
If they had many bulls, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אִם הָיוּ לָהֶם פָּרִים מְרוּבִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יחזקאל discussion and returns to quote the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the opening of רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה about having many bulls, to begin discussing it.

steps.title: A ברייתא quotes a פסוק about the flour for a bull and a ram
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes יחזקאל 46:7, which gives an איפה of flour for the bull and an איפה for the ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'And an איפה for the bull and an איפה for the ram he shall make as a מנחה, and for the lambs as much as he can afford, and a הין of oil for each איפה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts by quoting a פסוק from יחזקאל. This is setup: the next line will point out a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to give the same amount of flour, one איפה, to both the bull and the ram. That detail is what רבי שמעון is about to question. This ברייתא is the source for his opinion that the משנה just quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: A large dry measure of flour
A flour offering that comes along with an animal offering here
A liquid measure, used here for oil
As much as he can afford

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And an ephah for the bull and an ephah for the ram
he shall make as a meal offering,
and for the lambs as much as his hand can reach,
and a hin of oil for each ephah."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 46:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 25 quoted the opening of רבי שמעון's words in the משנה. Now the גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows the source for his opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in יחזקאל lists one איפה of flour for the bull and one איפה for the ram.

steps.title: רבי שמעון asks how a bull and a ram could get the same amount
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון points out that the Torah does not give bulls and rams the same amount of flour, so the פסוק cannot mean that literally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: Is the amount for bulls and rams really the same?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון raises a problem. The פסוק gives a bull and a ram the same amount, but we know their amounts are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the Torah, a bull's מנחה is three-tenths of an איפה, and a ram's is two-tenths. So reading the פסוק as a rule about measurements would go against the Torah. This is the same kind of hard פסוק in יחזקאל that the גמרא was discussing earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure, the amount of flour required
'Is it really so?', a word that opens a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying that יחזקאל made a mistake. His question shows that the פסוק must be teaching something other than measurements.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
Is the measure for bulls and rams
really one and the same?
phrases.notes: In the Torah a bull gets three-tenths of an ephah of flour and a ram gets two-tenths (במדבר 15:6, 9).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מִדַּת פָּרִים וְאֵילִים אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: He challenges the plain meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of יחזקאל 46:7, which gives an equal איפה to the bull and the ram
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah gives different amounts for a bull and a ram, so the פסוק cannot be setting equal measurements.

steps.title: Better one bull with its נסכים than many without
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that the פסוק teaches what to do when there is not enough for the נסכים. Bring one bull with its נסכים instead of all the bulls without נסכים. He then starts a second case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if they had many bulls but not enough for the נסכים, they should bring one bull with its נסכים, and not offer all of them without נסכים. And if they had...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers his own question. The פסוק is about choosing what to bring when there is not enough for everything. The last words begin a new case that continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'an איפה for the bull' teach that one bull should be brought together with its proper offering, even if this means bringing fewer bulls. Offering an animal fully, with its נסכים, matters more than the number of animals. This is the source for רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה about having many bulls.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour, oil, and wine that come along with an animal offering
Many bulls, all the bulls needed that day
They will be offered

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, if there is not enough for the נסכים, bring fewer animals with their נסכים rather than all the animals without them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the source of רבי שמעון's rule in the משנה. It also shows another hard פסוק in יחזקאל being explained without any conflict with the Torah.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that if they had
many bulls
but there were no libations for them,
they should bring one bull and its libations,
and they should not offer all of them without libations.
And if they had...

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שֶׁאִם הָיוּ לָהֶם פָּרִים מְרוּבִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge in step 27 by reading the פסוק a different way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: it is about priorities when funds are short, not about measurements.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to set an equal measure of flour for a bull and a ram.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that one bull with its נסכים is better than many bulls without נסכים.
